points.response: Consent exists on the 23:03 messages (F7, F8) but RD-5 exempts only the route change the rider actually agreed to, namely 'go round via Bedok South Avenue 3'; the GPS segment at 23:06–23:12 wanders up to 974 m off the optimal route and the trip finished 3.2 km long (F3, F1), so consent cannot cover track the rider never approved.

RD-3 only excuses a passenger-named stop that produces no off-route segment; here the very segment in dispute (F3, +2.96 km) exists on the record, so the passenger's naming of Bedok South Avenue 3 does not erase the measured off-route mileage.

I do not contest that the chat record is complete and timestamped (F9); completeness only proves when the messages were sent, not that the rider's agreement extended to the full 2.96 km off-route excursion shown in F3.

Band 4 (30–39 km/h) is outside the band 1–2 severe-congestion range that RD-4(b) recognises, no incident was recorded anywhere near the route (F13), and RD-4(b) cannot exempt a segment on its own — so F11 cannot convert an unexplained 2.96 km deviation into 'reasonable cause'.

I accept the mapping residues point: the segment is 2.96 km (F3) and only that measured segment is refundable, so I reduce my ask from $4.45 (3.2 km) to $4.17–$4.18 (2.96 km × $34.84 ÷ 24.7 km per F6).

I make no FARE-1 claim for waiting or add-ons (F6, F5 shows $0.00 waiting and no surge); my claim is the metered distance overcharge caused by the deviation under RD-2, which is a separate head from FARE-1.
I agree time and waiting units are not refundable, which is why my revised figure is the distance element only: 2.96 km × ($34.84 ÷ 24.7 km) ≈ $4.18 (F3, F6, F1), not the whole $53.17.

The rider's clean 90-day record (F15) is not in dispute and is not needed for the finding; the finding rests on the GPS off-route segment (F3) and the metered excess (F4), and only then does the driver's 2 upheld route disputes (F16) support the add-on flag under RD-6.

A deviation exists on the track, but RD-1 asks whether it is explained, and this one is: the driver proposed the specific diversion at 23:03 (F7) and the rider replied "Sure, go ahead." at 23:03 (F8), before the 23:06 segment start (F3), so the segment falls to be assessed under RD-5/RD-3 rather than condemned under RD-1 alone.

The meter arithmetic is right but RD-2 only bites on unexempt segments, and the single segment here is the very diversion the rider authorised in F8 before it began (F3, F7); with that segment exempt the refundable distance base is zero, not 2.96 km.

The rider did name a place, and RD-3(a) treats a rider-accepted reroute as not a deviation; nothing in RD-5 caps consent by kilometres, and her words in F8 answer the exact proposal in F7, so the segment is exempt as agreed rather than as later re-measured by the rider.

Conceded: band 4 (F11) is not band 1–2, no incident is recorded (F13) and the weather was fair (F14), so RD-4(a) is unavailable and RD-4(b) gives no standalone exemption — the driver's justification rests wholly on the rider's own consent, not on traffic.

The $4.45 (F4) is a billing arithmetic figure, not an entitlement: RD-2 measures refund from the unexempt segments' extra_km, and F3 puts the whole segment at 2.96 km while F1's 3.2 km excess leaves roughly 0.24 km of map-matching residue that RD-2 expressly does not refund.

F16 shows 2 upheld route disputes and is admissible only as the add-on basis for flag_account under RD-6, never as the main finding; on the merits the segment is covered by the rider's own pre-segment message in F8.
